## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `--exclude` flag needs an `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` environment default, because the project's cli-flags policy requires one for every newly added flag. The matching and the tests behave as described for the paths this review traced.

## Changes
This pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` option. `collect` now skips, and logs, files whose base name matches any of the patterns. The change also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md` and adds parser, `collect` and end-to-end archive tests, plus a new unused fixture file, `tests/fixtures/hostile-review.txt`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Take the --exclude default from ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE — With `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE=*.log` set and no `--exclude` flag, files are still archived, because the default is the hard-coded `default=[]`. This breaks `.claude/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11`: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable". — CI jobs that set options through the environment cannot apply exclusions, which defeats the reason the policy gives for the rule. — Fix: Choose a separator for the list (for example `os.pathsep` or a comma), parse `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` into the default, and add the variable to the `docs/flags.md:7` entry.
